decisions.statement: A token is refreshed at `https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token`.
Usage is probed at `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage`.
A profile is probed at `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile`.
The OAuth client id is a constant rather than a value read from the environment.
The refresh buffer is five minutes.
A token expiring inside three hours is renewed by the upkeep.
The upkeep runs once an hour.
A token response names an access token that is not empty.
A token response names a refresh token that is not empty.
A token response names the seconds until that token expires.
A usage response names a five-hour window and a seven-day window.
A usage window names a utilization as a number.
A usage window names a reset key whose value may be null.
A profile response names an account uuid that is not empty.
A profile response names an email as an optional field.
A body with keys a wire shape does not name still parses.
A key a wire shape does not name is kept on the parsed value.
A wire shape refuses a number that is NaN.
A wire shape refuses a number that is infinite.
A status of 500 or above is classified as not terminal.
A status of 429 is classified with the code `rate_limited`.
The code `invalid_grant` is terminal.
The code `invalid_client` is terminal.
A code the terminal set does not name is not terminal.
A terminal classification needs a status from 400 through 499.
A body the JSON parser refuses is classified as not terminal.
A body with no OAuth error envelope is classified as not terminal.
An absent `error` key is classified with no code.
An absent `error_description` key is classified with no description.
A retry-allowed instant is the moment handed in plus a backoff.
A `Retry-After` of whole seconds sets the backoff in milliseconds.
A backoff read from `Retry-After` is capped at five hours.
A missing `Retry-After` backs off five seconds.
A blank `Retry-After` backs off the default instead.
A `Retry-After` no greater than zero backs off the default instead.
A `Retry-After` the number parser refuses backs off the default instead.
A caller may hand in a backoff other than the default.
A gate with no attempt recorded allows a re-poll.
A re-poll inside sixty seconds of the last attempt is skipped.
A re-poll sixty seconds after the last attempt is allowed.
An open breaker skips a re-poll whatever the last attempt was.
A breaker opens for five minutes when usage answers a rate limit.
A breaker whose instant has arrived skips nothing.
A breaker skip is decided before the minimum interval is read.
A recorded attempt moves the last attempt to the moment handed in.
A recorded rate limit moves the last attempt as a recorded attempt does.
A recorded attempt leaves the breaker instant unchanged.
A skip has the whole seconds left rounded up.
A refresh outcome that worked has the credential the refresh answered with.
A refresh outcome that failed says whether the failure is terminal.
A refresh outcome that failed names the sort of failure.
A refresh outcome that failed may have the status the refresh met.
Every instant this module works from is handed in by the caller.
A caller has the gate state between two decisions.
Nothing here reads a clock.
Nothing here fetches.
Nothing here reads a file.
Nothing here reads an index.
Nothing here writes a token.
Nothing here holds the gate state a decision is read from.
Nothing here reads a second account to answer about the account asked about.
A `Retry-After` holding an HTTP date backs off the default instead.
A skip reason is prose rather than a code a caller branches on.
An account met by a rate limit waits five minutes even where `Retry-After` says a shorter wait.
A usage window's utilization is unbounded above.
A refresh outcome is declared here while the token refresh sits outside this module.

definition: the OAuth exchange an account's credentials and usage arrive over
